contact.summary: The build is a different composition from the frame: Figma has a centred 'Let's talk' hero above a form-left, contact-cards-right split, while the build has no hero and puts the intro plus three method cards on the left with the form on the right. Fields, cards, copy, icons and the button all differ in size and styling, and the build's contact channels, '1,200+' Discord count, 24-hour reply and fake success message are unbacked claims.

findings.title: Form sends nothing but reports success and a 24-hour reply

findings.build: handleSubmit validates, then setTimeout(800) sets isSubmitted; no request is made (ContactView.vue:16-33). Success card 'Message Received!' / 'Thank you for reaching out, {name}. A SelahCue specialist will respond within 24 hours.' / 'Send Another Message' (ContactView.vue:78-85).
findings.evidence: ContactView.vue:26-32 (timer, no fetch); no contact endpoint anywhere in implementation/api (grep contact_message / contact_form / submit_contact finds nothing); LEGAL-DRAFT-NOTES 9.4: 'the form sends nothing (a timer fakes success)'
findings.decision: Until a delivery path exists, should the form be removed or disabled with an honest note, or wired to an endpoint? Whatever ships, the success copy must not promise a reply time (the build's 24 h and the spec's 1–2 business days are both unbacked).

findings.title: Form states and ARIA below the gap-fill spec
findings.figma: Only the default state is drawn; no frame for validation, submitting, success or error (MARKETING-SITE-HANDOFF 5). The states are specified in MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF 6b/6c.
findings.build: Spec items not built: the form has no aria-label='Contact us'; no aria-required on required fields (FormField sets only aria-invalid/aria-describedby for errors); the success card has no aria-live='polite' region; the textarea has no aria-label and its counter is not in aria-describedby; validation runs on submit only (spec: blur or submit); the submitting state shows a spinner but not the 'Sending…' label and hides the label (UiButton .content.hidden); no server-error or network-error banner or Retry; the 100-character limits on name and church are not enforced.
findings.evidence: grep for aria-required|aria-live|aria-label in ContactView.vue and FormField.vue returns only the password toggle label; ContactView.vue:16-33 and 77-87
findings.fix: Add aria-label='Contact us' on the form, aria-required='true' on name/email/message, an aria-live='polite' success region ('Your message has been sent'), aria-describedby from the textarea to the counter, blur validation, 'Sending…' button text, the 6b error banners once a send path exists, and maxlength 100 on name and church.

findings.title: FormField styling: two handoffs disagree and one decision has to settle it for Contact and the auth pages
findings.figma: Contact (497:124) and every auth frame draw the field label as Inter Medium 13 in the secondary text colour and the input well on the inset fill, 44 high (AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF 2.2 and 2.3).
findings.build: FormField.vue follows MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF 10a: label 14/600 in the primary text colour, input on --sc-elevated, 3px focus glow. It is used by Contact, Sign up, Forgot password, Sign in, Reset and the affiliate and admin settings pages.
findings.evidence: contact-10 (class B, follows 10a), signin-06 and signin-07 (class A, follow AUTH 2.3); the cited sections quote opposite values; reported by the code review of PR 171 (finding 6)
findings.decision: Uma: which spec governs FormField for Contact and the auth pages together? If AUTH-LANDING 2.3: the auth variant (signin-06, signin-07) is built and contact-10 flips from class B to class A. If GAP-FILL 10a: signin-06 and signin-07 become class B citing it, and the frames are the ones to redraw. Settle it before the shared-components ticket (FormField) and the auth ticket finish.

findings.build: ChangelogView.vue:60 maps fixed to variant 'warn', which UiBadge does not define (UiBadge.vue:6 validator allows live / preview / ready / ndi / featured / new): 'FIXED' renders with no background or border and --sc-text ink, and Vue logs a prop-validation warning in dev. 'improved' uses 'ndi' (cyan #38bdf8 on info-soft) instead of brand.

findings.fix: Fixed -> variant 'ready' (warn-soft background, --sc-warn ink); Improved -> 'featured' (accent) or a dedicated tone matching #5b6bd6; New -> 'preview'; add a test that every UiBadge variant used in a view is defined.
